Hi Ho, Hi Ho - its off to Maine I go...

I Row, I Row - its off to Maine I Row...

used it all up yesterday writing my

Maine. Maine will kill my car.

(4) Hopefully Sometimes all I need to heal and cure 
Is a little rest and peace in my own back yard
A lone by myself without anybody fucking with me...
Now... could I get that please ???

---

There is only one person on this Earth who I have ever truly revealed myself to...
To everyone else I'm just a voice on a video, 
Telephone, a picture on a business card, a paragraph
in an email on a page in a book, 
That's been my choice and has led to a 
hollow existence... a collection of bits and 
pieces that could never accurately potray what 
is embodied in the whole... I'm trying to 
change that. If I can then I think that 
I shall find the fulfillment that my 
heart is now seeking... if I can't then 
let my failures act as a warning to 
anyone who happens to read this. and if I 
do succeed, then look towards me for hope and 
inspiration so that you might follow my 
lead carving out your own path 
footsteps... within the mold and contours of your 
own footprints. 

Yet Regardless of where my fate lies
whatever path this where I end up
on this great journey that is life just 
know that there is wisdom to be found 
in my story... in ALL of OUR
stories.
Much love,
Tom

cards.typed_words:
The Quick Version:

I've been writing poems meant to be used as song lyrics ever since I was 17 years old and heard Bob Dylan's LIKE A ROLLING STONE on the radio in my father's minivan. Shortly after that I got drunk, blacked out and totaled the minivan when I hit a telephone pole at a rather high rate of speed. I crawled away and was largely unhurt but the engine was now riding shotgun. A foot to my left and I'd have been dead. If my friend came with me then today he would have no legs. That's when I became a public servant and dedicated my life to trying to making a difference in this world. I've been doing that for the last 18 years or so... on my own dime... full-time... all while hiding behind a computer screen... and now it's time to show you what I have got... no more hiding  -  I'm looking to take it LIVE to THE PEOPLE, THE MUSICIANS AND THE SINGERS THEMSELVES.

I put out a book of 130 poems (with commentary) inviting musicians from all over the world to turn my words into songs. That was in 2008. I didn't have any songs at this point. I put videos of my poems on YouTube and found artists (or artists found them) and...

Today I have had 130 songs made from my lyrics. That's about seven hours' worth of original music, right there. The enclosed CD has 22 of them  -  a nice assorted sampler. My website is filled with goodies...

My current book of poems waiting for music now has over 400 poems in it. At least 20 albums worth of songs are just waiting for musicians and singers. I want to start by creating or taking over a bar or venue and naming it SONGWRITERS' or joining a current establishment where I can use this place as a central location to create new songs by day (with audience participation and feedback, of course) in person and have musicians play the songs [...cut for the check]

cards.typed_words:
COLLABRHYTHM COLLABTUNES.COM
The 120 songs he wrote all the lyrics for and then asked singers and musicians from all over the world to turn his words into songs proves it can be done. He's got the lyrics to 250 more songs just waiting to be added to that collection!!! But what if instead of using YouTube as our platform - what if we took it to a physical location and yet still let the online audience participate?

KEITH RICHARDS
BOB DYLAN
DAVID BOWIE
ROGER WATERS
DAVID CROSBY

It's a little sick and twisted, I know, but that's just the way my mind works. I never put anyone on this list from The Who, yet bass player John Entwistle passed away just about a month ago and drummer Keith Moon died what seems like a lifetime ago. You just never know when it's your time to go. My heart goes out to the families of anyone who has left this earth but I admit that the thought of the possibility of lead singer Roger Daltrey or singer and composer Pete Townshend dying instead of John Entwistle was deeply saddening. This book is dedicated to me. I lived it and breathed it and spoke it and seen it. I could have concocted a story so beautiful and courageous that people would have erected statues in my honor for it. Sorry guys and gals. Nothing but me.

Some people like writings which are very easy to follow. We are taught to worship law and order yet law and order strip us of freedom.. Welcome to non-chronological and illogical. You are lucky to get years let alone dates. Law and order takes away freedom. My friends, I'm here, there and everywhere. No rhyme no reason: well, actually there's a whole lot of rhymes and even more reasons but that will come beginning in the second sentence of my dedication and also the future. I have a job and I go to school and write poetry and attempt to be the nicest kid you know. Dedicating complete focus and attention is impossible - just ask my ex girlfriend.

A poetic life is so hard to lead
When distracted by sloth and greed
You just meet your need
As you pretend to succeed

Wear a false face
Make decisions in haste
When life quickens the pace
Just race the race

Finish first and someone must finish last
History teaches to remember the past
In the life we know the sun fades too fast
As soon as we turn the shadow's been cast

cards.typed_words:
An old gentleman wanders into a bar and sits himself down next to a young lady wearing gray pants with vertical stripes. Her hair is short and tucked neatly inside her matching derby hat. She's trying hard to smile but something seems to be troubling her. You don't have to be a doctor to notice a thing like that. The man casually walks over to her and explains to her that he has some experience in helping people solve their problems. Thinking it to be another cheesy pick-up line, the young woman denies that something is bothering her.

"Nothing's wrong," she says as she takes a sip of her colored refreshment (aptly named a green dinosaur).
"Surely something is playing on your mind...why don't you tell me why you appear as if you have lost something."
"I haven't lost anything..."
"Then perhaps you have found yourself involved with something of an unpleasant nature?"
"That is correct...however, it is not just necessarily me who has the problem."

"Go on my dear."
"Well, you see, I have begun to notice that my college has many female professors and yet we spend all our time studying male authors. I feel trapped in this patriarchal society. I mean we only spent one week on Emily Dickinson and we spent two weeks on some poem written by a guy named J. Alfred Proofrock. And my teacher was a woman. If it was a genre then I would label it such a tragedy."

"So you feel that female authors are inadequately represented and unappreciated in the literary world?" The creeky man crossed his legs as he pulled a pencil out from the chest pocket of his suitcoat.
"Oh absolutely! Just scan any silibi."
"First off, tell me about your home life...are you married?"
"No, do you see a ring on my finger?"
"Are you presently with somebody?"
"No, I was with someone but it didn't work out."
"I see. [...cut for the check]
